Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue "Compiler hangs when a parameter default value uses the natural type of its own method group" (#86348) at dotnet/roslyn
Events.RelatedBody:
**Version Used**: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 4.8.0, 4.14.0, 5.0.0, 5.6.0, 5.9.0, 5.13.0-1.26511.1, and the compiler of the .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148

## Steps to Reproduce

Compile the following code:

```cs
class C
{
    void M(object a = M) { }
}
```

The compilation never completes: `dotnet build` and `Compilation.GetDiagnostics()` hang, using a CPU core.

Standalone repro with the Roslyn API:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp" Version="5.9.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

```cs
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp;

var compilation = CSharpCompilation.Create(
    "Repro",
    [CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText("class C { void M(object a = M) { } }")],
    [MetadataReference.CreateFromFile(typeof(object).Assembly.Location)],
    new CSharpCompilationOptions(OutputKind.DynamicallyLinkedLibrary));

var task = Task.Run(() => compilation.GetDiagnostics());
Console.WriteLine(task.Wait(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10)) ? "Completed" : "GetDiagnostics() did not complete after 10 seconds");
```

Other inputs that hang (all with `LangVersion` 10 or later):

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `class C { void M(object a = M) { } }` | Hang |
| `class C { void M(int a = M == null) { } }` | Hang |
| `class C { void M(bool a = M == M) { } }` | Hang |
| `class C { void M(int a = 0, int b = M == null) { } }` | Hang |
| `void M(int a = M == null) { }` (top-level local function) | Hang |
| `class C { void M(int a = M == null) { } }` with `LangVersion` 9 | CS0019 |
| `class C { void M(int a = M is null) { } }` | CS0837 |
| `class C { void M() { } void N(int a = M == null) { } }` | CS1736 |

The input was found by fuzzing ([meziantou/Meziantou.Analyzer#1775](https://github.com/meziantou/Meziantou.Analyzer/issues/1775)). The original input was reduced to `void value(int a = value == null) { }`.

## Expected Behavior

The compilation completes and reports an error, such as CS1736 (`Default parameter value for 'a' must be a compile-time constant`), as it does when the method group refers to another method.

## Actual Behavior

The compilation never completes. The thread waits for itself:

1. `SourceComplexParameterSymbolBase.get_DefaultSyntaxValue` binds the default value of `a`.
2. Binding `M == null` (or the conversion of `M` to `object`) asks for the natural type of the method group `M` (`FunctionTypeSymbol.GetInternalDelegateType`).
3. `Binder.GetMethodGroupOrLambdaDelegateType` reads `ParameterSymbol.HasExplicitDefaultValue` of the parameters of `M`, so it reads the default value of `a` again.
4. The default value of `a` is not complete yet, so `SymbolCompletionState.SpinWaitComplete` waits for it forever, on the thread that is computing it.

It does not hang with C# 9, as method groups have no natural type before C# 10.

## Problem

When dotnetup is already configured, `dotnetup init` preselects the configured access mode and labels it `(default)`. For example, if `dotnetup.config.json` contains `"accessMode": "none"`, the form shows `None  (default)` on Windows, even though the platform default for new setups on Windows is `Everywhere`.

This happens because `InitDefaultsResolver.GetDefaultAccessMode` gives a supported configured mode priority over the platform default. `InitFormModel.BuildAccessModeField` then uses that mode as the field's `DefaultIndex`, which is rendered with the `(default)` suffix. Users who reconfigure can't tell which mode dotnetup recommends for their platform.

## Proposal

Keep preselecting the configured mode, so accepting the form without edits preserves the current setup. Label the two modes separately:

- `(current)` on the configured mode
- `(recommended)` on the platform default (`Everywhere` on Windows; `Shell` elsewhere when a supported shell is detected, otherwise `None`)

When the two are the same, show a single label. "Changed from default" highlighting should compare against the current (preselected) mode.

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths" (#43153)

Issues.Title: Compiler hangs when a parameter default value uses the natural type of its own method group
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 4.8.0, 4.14.0, 5.0.0, 5.6.0, 5.9.0, 5.13.0-1.26511.1, and the compiler of the .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148

## Steps to Reproduce

Compile the following code:

```cs
class C
{
    void M(object a = M) { }
}
```

The compilation never completes: `dotnet build` and `Compilation.GetDiagnostics()` hang, using a CPU core.

Standalone repro with the Roslyn API:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp" Version="5.9.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

```cs
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp;

var compilation = CSharpCompilation.Create(
    "Repro",
    [CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText("class C { void M(object a = M) { } }")],
    [MetadataReference.CreateFromFile(typeof(object).Assembly.Location)],
    new CSharpCompilationOptions(OutputKind.DynamicallyLinkedLibrary));

var task = Task.Run(() => compilation.GetDiagnostics());
Console.WriteLine(task.Wait(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10)) ? "Completed" : "GetDiagnostics() did not complete after 10 seconds");
```

Other inputs that hang (all with `LangVersion` 10 or later):

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `class C { void M(object a = M) { } }` | Hang |
| `class C { void M(int a = M == null) { } }` | Hang |
| `class C { void M(bool a = M == M) { } }` | Hang |
| `class C { void M(int a = 0, int b = M == null) { } }` | Hang |
| `void M(int a = M == null) { }` (top-level local function) | Hang |
| `class C { void M(int a = M == null) { } }` with `LangVersion` 9 | CS0019 |
| `class C { void M(int a = M is null) { } }` | CS0837 |
| `class C { void M() { } void N(int a = M == null) { } }` | CS1736 |

The input was found by fuzzing ([meziantou/Meziantou.Analyzer#1775](https://github.com/meziantou/Meziantou.Analyzer/issues/1775)). The original input was reduced to `void value(int a = value == null) { }`.

## Expected Behavior

The compilation completes and reports an error, such as CS1736 (`Default parameter value for 'a' must be a compile-time constant`), as it does when the method group refers to another method.

## Actual Behavior

The compilation never completes. The thread waits for itself:

1. `SourceComplexParameterSymbolBase.get_DefaultSyntaxValue` binds the default value of `a`.
2. Binding `M == null` (or the conversion of `M` to `object`) asks for the natural type of the method group `M` (`FunctionTypeSymbol.GetInternalDelegateType`).
3. `Binder.GetMethodGroupOrLambdaDelegateType` reads `ParameterSymbol.HasExplicitDefaultValue` of the parameters of `M`, so it reads the default value of `a` again.
4. The default value of `a` is not complete yet, so `SymbolCompletionState.SpinWaitComplete` waits for it forever, on the thread that is computing it.

It does not hang with C# 9, as method groups have no natural type before C# 10.

Stack trace (Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.9.0, trimmed):


Issues.Title: Drain compilation event queue in compiler-only analysis
Issues.Body:
### Problem

For compiler-only single-file analysis, `CompilationWithAnalyzers` reuses the root `_compilation`. Binding the file enqueues `SymbolDeclaredCompilationEvent`s on that compilation's event queue, but this path never reads the queue. The events and the semantic models they reference stay alive until the project changes.

On a large solution in the language server, a heap dump showed one project's queue holding 20,217 events.

### Fix

Drain the root compilation's event queue once the compiler-only single-file analysis completes.

A new test was also added which fails without the change (14 events left) and passes with it.

Issues.Body:
Fix six defects in the existing handwritten protocol models:

- Use the standard `isPreferred` and `notebookDocument` JSON property names.
- Represent workspace-symbol tags as an array.

Issues.Title: FSA diagnostics cache ignores analyzer filter changes on an unchanged project
Issues.Body:
### Description

Closed-file full-solution analysis (FSA) diagnostics can remain stale when compiler or analyzer diagnostic scopes change without changing the project snapshot. Fresh diagnostic pulls continue to return results computed using the previous analyzer filter.

Observed with the Roslyn language server bundled by dotnet/vscode-csharp:
- Version: `5.14.0-1.26552.2`
- Source revision: `eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4`
- Environment: VS Code on macOS, standalone C# extension (without C# Dev Kit)

The same cache implementation was also present in upstream `main` when investigated.

### Reproduction

Use a closed C# file containing both compiler and analyzer diagnostics, for example the [vscode-csharp diagnostics fixture](https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-csharp/blob/main/test/lsptoolshost/integrationTests/testAssets/slnWithCsproj/src/app/diagnostics.cs).

Keep `dotnet.backgroundAnalysis.analyzerDiagnosticsScope` set to `fullSolution` throughout:

1. Set `dotnet.backgroundAnalysis.compilerDiagnosticsScope` to `fullSolution`. Pull workspace diagnostics to populate the cache.
2. Change compiler scope to `none`, without editing any files, and pull diagnostics again.
3. Add and save whitespace in an unrelated C# file in the same project, then pull diagnostics again.
4. Change compiler scope back to `fullSolution`, without another edit, and pull diagnostics again.
5. Add and save another whitespace edit in the unrelated file, then pull diagnostics again.

The diagnostic target remained closed, and the language-server PID remained unchanged throughout the controlled reproduction.

| Step | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Both scopes full solution | 5 diagnostics, including compiler warning `CS0219` | 5 |
| Compiler scope changed to none | 4 diagnostics, without `CS0219` | Still 5, including `CS0219` |
| Unrelated whitespace edit saved | 4 | 4 |
| Compiler scope changed back to full solution | 5, including `CS0219` | Still 4, missing `CS0219` |
| Second unrelated whitespace edit saved | 5 | 5 |

The five initial diagnostic codes were `CA1822`, `CS0219`, `IDE0005`, `IDE0059`, and `IDE0130`.

### Configuration and diagnostic freshness

This was reproduced while removing unnecessary server restarts from vscode-csharp integration tests. To rule out client timing and cached diagnostic collections, the experiment:

- Awaited forwarding of the final configuration notification.
- Sent `workspace/waitForAsyncOperations` after that notification to wait for server processing/background work.
- Requested full workspace diagnostic reports by omitting previous result IDs.
- Inspected newly returned reports through the normal language-client diagnostic pipeline, rather than relying only on existing VS Code diagnostic collections.

The returned full reports themselves contained the stale diagnostic set. Restarting the server, or changing the project snapshot through the unrelated edit, made the scopes take effect.

### Suspected root cause

[`AbstractWorkspaceDocumentDiagnosticSource.FullSolutionAnalysisDiagnosticSource`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4/src/LanguageServer/Protocol/Handler/Diagnostics/DiagnosticSources/AbstractWorkspaceDocumentDiagnosticSource.cs#L35) caches diagnostics using:

```csharp
ConditionalWeakTable<Project, AsyncLazy<ILookup<DocumentId, DiagnosticData>>>
```

The cached `AsyncLazy` captures `analyzerFilter` when it calls `GetDiagnosticsForIdsAsync`. However, `analyzerFilter` is not part of the cache identity. A subsequent source for the same `Project` instance but a different filter therefore reuses diagnostics calculated under the previous filter.

[`WorkspaceDocumentsAndProjectDiagnosticSourceProvider`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4/src/LanguageServer/Protocol/Handler/Diagnostics/DiagnosticSourceProviders/WorkspaceDocumentsAndProjectDiagnosticSourceProvider.cs) derives the filter from the current compiler/analyzer FSA scopes, so configuration changes can alter the filter without replacing the project instance.

The project-level diagnostic source does not use this particular cache; this report concerns closed-document FSA diagnostics.

### Suggested fix and regression coverage

Include `AnalyzerFilter` in the cache identity while preserving weak references to project instances and sharing cached computations across documents for the same project/filter.

Add regression tests that populate the real FSA source cache, then independently change compiler and analyzer scopes on the same project snapshot, in both directions, without file edits or server restarts. The existing [FSA on/off tests](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4/src/LanguageServer/ProtocolUnitTests/Diagnostics/PullDiagnosticTests.cs#L2296) toggle both scopes together; they do not exercise a changed analyzer filter while FSA remains enabled.

### Impact

Users can continue seeing diagnostics that should have been disabled, or fail to see newly enabled diagnostics, until the project snapshot changes. This also currently prevents removing per-case server restarts from the closed-file diagnostics integration tests in dotnet/vscode-csharp.

Issues.Title: Use current source trees for definition locations after edits
Issues.Body:
Frozen partial semantics can return a symbol whose source span belongs to an older target document. The LSP handler resolves its document ID in the current solution and reports the wrong line or column after an edit.

Reject source locations whose trees differ from the current solution and retry full semantics. Unchanged target trees keep the frozen-semantic fast path from #72714.

The regression explicitly enables partial semantics, which production enables but test workspaces disable by default. It covers definition and type-definition, line and column movement, both LSP workspace modes, and C#/VB.

Validation:

- All 16 new cases fail without the fix and pass with it.
- All 72 definition tests pass, with no skips.
- The standalone LSP probe improves from 72/84 to 84/84 exact locations. Edited answers equal a clean restart.
- Affected builds pass with analyzers enabled. Whitespace and diff checks pass.

Fixes #86331

Issues.Title: Simplify ProjectData atomic write and temp directory routing
Issues.Body:
Alternative to https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86210

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3715
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3541
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3564

### Motivation & Background

1. **Why `ReplaceOrMove` existed originally and why `File.Replace` failed (`#3541`, `#3715`)**
   - `ReplaceOrMove` (`File.Replace` → `File.Move` → `File.Replace`) was originally written when the task targeted `netstandard2.0`, which did not have `File.Move(string, string, bool overwrite)`.
   - On Windows, `File.Replace` calls Win32 `ReplaceFileW`, which opens the destination for metadata/attribute transfer and requires the replacement and destination paths to resolve on the same volume without cross-volume directory reparse points. This caused failures on ReFS volumes / Dev Drives ([microsoft/vscode-dotnettools#3541](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3541): `Access to the path is denied` / `Unable to remove the file to be replaced`) and when directories are redirected across volumes via Windows directory symbolic links ([microsoft/vscode-dotnettools#3715](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3715): `Unable to move the replacement file to the file to be replaced`).

2. **Why `File.Move(tempPath, outputPath, overwrite: true)` replaces `ReplaceOrMove`**
   - `Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Tasks` now targets `$(NetRoslynSourceBuild)` (`net11.0`), where `File.Move(source, dest, overwrite: true)` is available directly.
   - `File.Move(..., overwrite: true)` uses `MoveFileExW` with `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING` (and `MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED`) on Windows and `rename(2)` (with cross-device fallback) on Unix, replacing the 3-step `ReplaceOrMove` helper in a single call.

3. **Why `IntermediateOutputPath` temp-file routing is only needed for project-folder `.lscache` writes (`#3564`)**
   - Staging the transient `.tmp` side-file under `$(IntermediateOutputPath)` (`obj/`) was introduced solely for source-tree hygiene when `.lscache` is written next to the `.csproj` (`EnableProjectDataInProjectFolder=true`), so transient `.tmp` files do not briefly appear in the source tree where Git, File Explorer, or file watchers can observe them.
   - For **user-folder caches** (`~/.local/share` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%`) and **inner-build `.slice` files** (which already live under `obj/`), routing the `.tmp` file through `$(IntermediateOutputPath)` is unnecessary. Worse, on Linux/macOS (such as DevContainers or Codespaces where `/workspaces/.../obj` and `~/.local/share/...` are on different mounts), `Path.GetPathRoot` returns `"/"` for both paths, causing the writer to stage the `.tmp` file in `obj/` and then attempt a cross-mount move into the user-folder cache ([microsoft/vscode-dotnettools#3564](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3564): `Invalid cross-device link`).
   - By omitting `IntermediateOutputPath` on `_WriteProjectDataSlice`, `_WriteProjectDataUserFolder`, and `_MergeProjectDataSlicesUserFolder`, transient `.tmp` files for slice and user-folder writes are staged directly beside `outputPath` on the destination filesystem.

4. **Improved failure diagnostics (`#3541`)**
   - Previously, `WriteProjectDataSliceTask` and `MergeProjectDataSlicesTask` logged only `ProjectFilePath` and `ex.Message` (producing warnings like `ProjectData: failed to write project-data file for Foo.csproj: Unable to remove the file to be replaced.` with no target path, exception type, or stack trace).
   - Both tasks now log `ResolvedOutputPath`, `ProjectFilePath`, and the full `ex` so any future I/O failure is immediately actionable.

Issues.Title: Suboptimal codegen for `is` pattern: binary search prevents JIT from using a bit test
Issues.Body:
Since .NET 9, the JIT folds a chain of `==` comparisons against constants into a single `bt` with a constant mask. Roslyn lowers the equivalent `is` pattern to a binary search over the constants, so the JIT no longer sees that chain.

Repro: [compiler-explorer](https://compiler-explorer.com/z/4zPMoq1xP)

```csharp
public static int N_0(char c)
{
    if (c is < ' ' or > '~'
        or '"'
        or '\\'
        or '&'
        or '\''
        or '+'
        or '<'
        or '>'
        or '`')
        return 1;
    return 0;
}

public static int N_1(char c)
{
    if (c < ' ' || c > '~'
        || c == '"'
        || c == '\\'
        || c == '&'
        || c == '\''
        || c == '+'
        || c == '<'
        || c == '>'
        || c == '`')
        return 1;
    return 0;
}    
```

**`N_0` decompiled, the relevant part:**
```csharp
if (c <= '+')
{
    if (c <= '&')
    {
        if (c == '"' || c == '&')
            goto label_8;
    }
    else if (c == '\'' || c == '+')
        goto label_8;
}
else if (c <= '>')
{
    if (c == '<' || c == '>')
        goto label_8;
}
else if (c == '\\' || c == '`')
    goto label_8;
```

Both methods start with the same range check. The relevant part is what follows it.

**`N_0` (IL size: 84 bytes, code size: 89 bytes):**
```asm
G_M44197_IG05:
       cmp      eax, 43
       jle      SHORT G_M44197_IG07
       cmp      eax, 62
       jle      SHORT G_M44197_IG06
       cmp      eax, 92
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       cmp      eax, 96
       jne      SHORT G_M44197_IG09
       jmp      SHORT G_M44197_IG03
G_M44197_IG06:
       cmp      eax, 60
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       cmp      eax, 62
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       jmp      SHORT G_M44197_IG09
G_M44197_IG07:
       cmp      eax, 38
       jle      SHORT G_M44197_IG08
       cmp      eax, 39
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       cmp      eax, 43
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       jmp      SHORT G_M44197_IG09
G_M44197_IG08:
       cmp      eax, 34
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       cmp      eax, 38
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
G_M44197_IG09:
       xor      eax, eax
       pop      rbp
       ret
```

**`N_1` (IL size: 54 bytes, code size: 52 bytes):**
```asm
G_M45220_IG05:
       add      eax, -34
       cmp      eax, 62
       ja       SHORT G_M45220_IG07
       mov      rcx, 0x4400000014000231
       bt       rcx, rax
       jb       SHORT G_M45220_IG03
G_M45220_IG07:
       xor      eax, eax
       pop      rbp
       ret
```

`N_0` does not get `bt` on .NET 9, 10 or 11 RC3, while `N_1` gets it on all three.

This is not specific to `is`. With the constants alone (no range checks), an `is` pattern, a `switch` statement and a switch expression all produce 77 bytes without `bt`, while the `||` chain produces 42 bytes.

The tree can also split a set that fits in one mask. For `is '"' or '\\' or '&' or '<' or '>' or '+'`, the JIT emits two `bt` instructions, one per half of the tree (68 bytes). The `||` chain gets one (42 bytes).

**Possible fix:** when all constants fit in a 64-bit window, Roslyn could emit a linear chain of `==` instead of the binary search. Larger sets would keep the binary search.

The trade-off is on runtimes without this optimization. On .NET 8, `N_1` is still smaller (68 vs 89 bytes), but it takes more comparisons on the worst path.

Issues.Title: [WIP] Fix CA2012 false positive for ValueTask in C# 14 extension
Issues.Body:
Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>CA2012 false positive when consuming ValueTask through a C# 14 extension block</issue_title>
> <issue_description>### Describe the bug
> 
> CA2012 reports a false positive when a returned `ValueTask<T>` is immediately consumed by an extension method declared using a C# 14 extension block.
> 
> The extension method awaits its receiver exactly once, and the caller immediately awaits the extension method's result. There is no stored or multiply consumed `ValueTask`. The equivalent traditional `this ValueTask<T>` extension method does not produce the warning.
> 
> This was already reported in the former analyzer repository:
> 
> - https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/issues/7784
> - https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/issues/7789
> 
> Both reports remain open. Filing here because the [repository consolidation notice](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/blob/archive/README.md) directs `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers` development and issues to `dotnet/sdk`.
> 
> ### To reproduce
> 
> The following minimal reproduction is adapted from the existing reports. Use a console project targeting `net10.0` with C# 14 or later and CA2012 enabled.
> 
> ```csharp
> using System.Threading.Tasks;
> 
> await GetValueAsync().ViaExtensionBlock(); // CA2012 on GetValueAsync()
> await GetValueAsync().ViaTraditionalExtension(); // No CA2012
> await Extensions.ViaExtensionBlock(GetValueAsync()); // No CA2012
> 
> static ValueTask<int> GetValueAsync() => new(42);
> 
> public static class Extensions
> {
>     extension(ValueTask<int> task)
>     {
>         public async ValueTask<int> ViaExtensionBlock() => await task;
>     }
> 
>     public static async ValueTask<int> ViaTraditionalExtension(
>         this ValueTask<int> task) => await task;
> }
> ```
> 
> If needed, enable the diagnostic explicitly in `.editorconfig`:
> 
> ```ini
> [*.cs]
> dotnet_diagnostic.CA2012.severity = warning
> ```
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> All three calls should be accepted. Each passes the returned `ValueTask<int>` directly to a method that awaits it exactly once.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The extension-block invocation produces CA2012:
> 
> > ValueTask instances returned from method calls should be directly awaited, returned, or passed as an argument to another method call.
> 
> The traditional extension-method and explicit static-call forms avoid the warning, as documented in the linked reports.
> 
> In our application, this occurs throughout chains such as `await authorizer.Ensure(request).Try(errorMapper)`. `Ensure` returns `ValueTask<Result<T, TError>>`, and `Try` is declared in an extension block with the implementation `(await task).Try(errorMapper)`.
> 
> ### Environment
> 
> Current affected application:
> - .NET SDK: `11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148`
> - Target framework: `net10.0`
> - Language version: `preview`
> - OS: Arch Linux, x64
> 
> The original report dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#7784 reproduced the issue with .NET SDK `10.0.101`. The minimal reproduction above is adapted from the existing reports; it has not been separately built with the current application's SDK.
> </issue_description>
> - Closes dotnet/sdk#56872
> 
> ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section)
> 
> <comments>
> </comments>
- Fixes #56872

Issues.Title: Fix cancellation rollback and Run API stdin handling
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #56332, targeting its branch rather than `main`.

- Run MSI manifest and pack rollback with a non-cancelled cleanup token, so cancellation of later work does not prevent uninstalling earlier successful changes or replace the original cancellation exception.
- Move Run API's synchronized `Console.In.ReadLine` onto a background worker and cancel the wait. `Console.In.ReadLineAsync(token)` otherwise blocks synchronously before returning. At most one read remains until CLI process exit; the synchronized reader is not disposed on cancellation.
- Add deterministic Windows installer-seam regressions, an out-of-process test with a real open redirected stdin pipe and cancellation after read entry, newline/blank-line/EOF protocol coverage, repeated Unix signals, and isolated Windows Ctrl+C cooperative/forced/repeated/suppression-lease coverage. Signals are delivered to dedicated helper processes, not the MTP host.

## Validation

- Red/green check: with the original three cancellation call sites restored, both MSI cases failed because rollback replaced the original exception, and the open-stdin test timed out without input. Restoring the fixes makes them pass.
- Redist-only build passed with no warnings or errors.
- `dotnet.Tests`: 17 selected cancellation and existing Run API compatibility cases passed on each of three runs.
- `Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils.Tests`: all three Windows lifecycle cases passed on each of three runs; seven Unix-only lifecycle/reaper cases were skipped on Windows.
- Existing live child-process cancellation regression passed.

MSI coverage uses deterministic native-operation seams and does not install real MSI packages. Unix signal coverage was added but could not be executed on this Windows host. The initial full-solution build encountered unrelated TemplateEngine missing-project and approval-file failures; validation used the successful redist-only build and focused test projects. The standard test-layout setup targets were run before existing Run API tests.

No changes to the original PR branch, ProcessReaper suppression semantics, shutdown handling, or stack metadata.

Progress on https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56948.

Backports the November 2026 Microsoft Trusted Root Program update from #56949 (commit f344df8e9372871a10f4e146cf802b520895801b) to `release/10.0.1xx` for December servicing.

This is not a clean cherry-pick because main uses MSTest `[DataRow]` attributes while this branch still uses xUnit `[InlineData]`. Conflicts in both trusted-roots test files were resolved by preserving xUnit and removing only the equivalent AAA Certificate Services baseline rows. No test-framework migration is included. The PEM updates and scoped LF-normalization rule are unchanged from the merged main update.

Validation on Windows: the redist build succeeded with zero warnings and zero errors, and all 46 trusted-roots tests passed, with no failures or skips. The built PEMs exactly match the committed main PEMs. TRX and binlogs were retained.

Local build options were `-warnNotAsError NU1903 /p:WarningsNotAsErrors=NU1903 /p:IlcUseEnvironmentalTools=true` after initializing the installed x64 C++ environment. No NU1903 warning was emitted on this branch. No dependency, checked-in warning-policy, or test-infrastructure changes are included.

CC @aortiz-msft, @dotnet/nuget-team

Issues.Title: Honor --no-update-check for built-in template availability notices
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #55386.

- Skip the built-in package availability task when template instantiation specifies `--no-update-check`, alongside the existing suppression of NuGet update checks.
- Preserve normal provider notices and uninstall guidance without the flag. Installation-time override guidance and `TemplatePackageDisplay` are unchanged.
- Add deterministic, in-process regression coverage using an older manually installed synthetic package and a newer built-in package from an `Optional workloads` provider. Exercise actual creation and dry-run, with and without update suppression; verify selected-package precedence, generated output, notice/uninstall guidance, and NuGet update-call suppression.
- Clarify the existing option's behavior in template-resolution documentation.

## Validation

- Before the fix: the two flag-off control cases passed; both `--no-update-check` cases failed because the built-in notice was still printed.
- After the fix: all **8** tests in `Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests.ParserTests.TemplateCommandTests` passed.
- Executed through `scripts/RunTests.cs` with `--skip-redist-check`; these tests run the freshly built command assembly in-process and do not consume an assembled SDK. TRX and build binlog retained locally.
- Full SDK/workload integration was not completed locally: cold redist builds were stopped due shared-machine memory pressure. No workloads or public NuGet template packages are needed for the new regression.

Issues.Title: Avoid mutating shared command metadata when rendering help
Issues.Body:
Fixes #52136.

## Summary

- Compute legacy option argument labels during rendering instead of setting `Option.HelpName`.
- Register display-only argument/description customizations while initializing the command tree, rather than replacing parent arguments, clearing package completion sources, or overwriting workload-version descriptions in the help writer.
- Keep template arguments hidden in shared definitions while explicitly including them in generic template help. Merge template choices into render-local option instances and shorten choice labels without modifying their options.
- Add shared managed/AOT regressions for metadata identity, completion sources, repeated/mixed-order help, legacy/current parsing, and list-reference display customization. Extend existing template-help snapshot tests to cover argument visibility, option identity, completion/parsing, and narrow/wide rendering order.

Existing displayed labels and legacy aliases remain supported. The intended behavioral change is that rendering help no longer affects later help, parsing, or completion; in particular, workload-version help retains its full synopsis after the parent command's help is displayed.

## Validation

All focused runs used `scripts/RunTests.cs`, single-node project builds (`-m:1 -p:BuildInParallel=false`), and the pinned repository SDK plus the matching runtime. The runner's concurrency arguments were temporary local validation changes and are not included in this PR. These are in-process tests of the freshly built assemblies; `--skip-redist-check` was used deliberately, not as evidence of a complete SDK layout.

| Focused suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests.ParserTests.HelpTests` | 37 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; existing snapshots unchanged |
| `dotnet.Tests` / `HelpRenderingTests` | 5 passed twice, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| `dotnet-aot.Tests` / shared `HelpRenderingTests` (`CLI_AOT` source build, not native-published) | 5 passed twice, 0 failed, 0 skipped |

All three project builds succeeded with **zero warnings/errors**. The tests exercise actual metadata identity, completion sources/results, repeated/mixed-order rendering, legacy/current parsing, hidden template arguments, merged choices, and width-dependent choice labels. TRX and build binlogs are retained under `artifacts/log/test-runs`.

The initial CI compile failures in build 1668372 were corrected: managed parser imports are conditional, the obsolete TemplateEngine import is removed, and nullable label assertions have explicit non-null guards. Local validation also corrected the shared test's missing Commands import and its nullable-boolean label expectation. Head `fca1e619dc9` contains these executable-tested corrections; older failing CI heads are not validation of this head.

**Remaining CI gate:** full rebuilt-SDK/platform validation and native-published AOT execution. No cold full redist or native publish was run locally. Source diff, XML, and changed documentation link-target checks also pass.

This PR is independent against `main`; it does not include the separate property-help, reference-description, or forwarding/escaping fixes.

Issues.Title: Show --property in dotnet build help
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #48742.

- Expose the existing property option only on `dotnet build`, with a localized description and `NAME=VALUE` hint.
- Display the canonical `-p, --property` help label without removing any accepted MSBuild aliases or changing property parsing/forwarding.
- Add rebuilt managed/AOT product help coverage, all six property aliases, repeated/semicolon-separated property forwarding, project-operand preservation, native help regression coverage and native/managed property-invocation parity tests.
- Update only `BuildJson`'s property description/visibility/help name in the existing CLI schema expectation. All aliases, arity, value type, other command expectations and `ReferenceJson` remain unchanged.

The broader MSBuild help policy in #49158 is out of scope. This is independent of #56969 and does not include that PR's commits, resource changes or reference-schema expectation changes.

## Validation

Validated corrected head **40e1692630809a93904538dc3a4b65f3980ed020** on Windows x64 after obtaining the serialized local build slot:

- **6/6 `CliSchemaTests` cases passed, 0 skipped**, including all five command-schema equality cases and schema generation. Before the schema expectation correction, all five equality cases executed: four passed and only `build` failed, showing the missing description/help name and stale `hidden:true` expectation.
- **7/7 CLI_AOT-source parser/help cases rerun and passed, 0 skipped**: `InvokeBuildHelp_ShowsPropertyOptionWithoutFallback` and all six `ParseBuildPropertyAliases_PreservesMultipleProperties` rows. These are source-built in-process tests, **not NativeAOT execution**.
- **6/6 source-built managed forwarding cases rerun and passed, 0 skipped**: `PropertyAliasesPreserveMultiplePropertyForwarding` for all six aliases. The bootstrap SDK supplied test-fixture infrastructure (`--version`) only; forwarding executed the rebuilt managed production methods.
- **19 unique focused cases passed in total**, preserving and rerunning all 13 earlier help/parser/forwarding cases alongside the six schema cases.
- Actual source-built managed `dotnet.dll build --help` previously exited **0**, displayed `-p, --property <NAME=VALUE>` and the localized-source description, and kept `--restoreProperty`/`--getProperty` hidden. It did not use bootstrap managed help; the latest commit changes only the test expectation.
- Hidden-option negative control: temporarily restoring the original `Hidden=true` behavior made the help regression fail for the missing property label. After restoring the fix, all seven CLI_AOT-source cases passed again. This is a controlled regression mutation, not a full baseline SDK build.
- Builds used **`/m:1 /p:UseSharedCompilation=false`**, with **0 warnings and 0 errors**. The local-only runner adjustment and fixture SDK junction were removed; `git diff --check` passes and the worktree is clean.
- Generated XLF for all 13 translation files was committed by [the successful `/updatexlf` workflow](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/42288247935) in ad23f70afcb80a8884b05dbecc0132bbc08c8a3c.
- **Full rebuilt-SDK and real native integration remain pending PR CI for the updated head.** No local full-redist build/native publish was run, no native skip is counted as evidence, and no all-platform/merge-ready claim is made.

Focused selections used the repository `scripts/RunTests.cs` entry point with `--skip-redist-check`, because these selected tests exercise source-built parser/schema/forwarding code in-process rather than the assembled SDK:

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet-aot.Tests\dotnet-aot.Tests.csproj --skip-redist-check --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~InvokeBuildHelp_ShowsPropertyOptionWithoutFallback|FullyQualifiedName~ParseBuildPropertyAliases_PreservesMultipleProperties'
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --skip-redist-check --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~CliSchemaTests|FullyQualifiedName~PropertyAliasesPreserveMultiplePropertyForwarding'
```

## Compatibility

Help metadata is changed only on `BuildCommandDefinition.ImplicitRestoreOptions.PropertiesOption`. The shared help builder registers a build-only display customization during `NormalizeRootOptions(rootCommand)` using its already-created local command tree; the lazy factory does not dereference the not-yet-initialized `Parser.RootCommand`. This fixes the startup regression found in review of the initial patch without introducing help-time definition mutation or relying on #52136.

All accepted aliases (`--property`, `-property`, `/property`, `/p`, `-p`, `--p`), arity, overwrite semantics and forwarding remain owned by the existing implementation. No AOT source/dependency closure, eligibility, or fallback changes are made. Native help is asserted on the source-built library; rebuilt managed/AOT help is covered through `dotnet.Tests`. The native harness's bootstrap SDK supplies managed fallback for the unchanged property-invocation comparison, not for new-help expectations.

Issues.Title: Escape literal output paths before forwarding to MSBuild
Issues.Body:
Fixes #49671.

## Summary

- Escape CLI-owned `--output` paths using the existing `MSBuildPropertyEscaping` utility (`ProjectCollection.Escape` plus MSBuild command-line comma/quote handling).
- Move shared output-path forwarding into managed command wiring for build, publish, clean, store, and VSTest. The AOT-safe definitions assembly gains no MSBuild dependency; build-backed commands retain their existing managed fallback.
- Preserve raw user `-p:` syntax, path normalization, the command-line-defined-output marker, and VSTest quote wrapping.
- Add 16 filesystem build/publish cases checking actual DLL, PDB, dependency, and runtimeconfig files at the requested paths. Cover relative/absolute paths, semicolon-containing working directories, literal `%3B`, `$`, quotes, commas, spaces, and trailing separators. Add forwarding tests, Unix-only double-quote/wildcard paths, and explicit-property syntax preservation.

Reuses the repository's existing MSBuild-backed helper rather than the ad-hoc escaping approach discussed in closed, unmerged #52582.

## Validation

Reproduced `MSB1006` with `dotnet publish --output 'out;put'` on both the installed .NET 10 SDK and the repository's .NET 12 bootstrap SDK before validating the fix.

[PR CI build 1668363](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1668363) rebuilt the SDK and ran the new regressions on Linux x64. The individual outcomes were verified directly in public Helix TRX artifacts, not inferred from build/check counts:

- **16/16** `OutputOptionWritesFilesToLiteralPath` cases passed: both build and publish wrote the expected files to the exact literal paths for every relative/absolute and trailing-separator combination. [CLI shard 3 TRX](https://helixr1107v0xdeko0k025g8.blob.core.windows.net/dotnet-sdk-refs-pull-56972-merge-e58c2099d21f4603a3/dotnet.Tests.dll.3/1/dotnet.Tests_net12.0_x64.trx?helixlogtype=result) — 387 passed, 0 failed.
- **16/16** `MSBuildOptionExtensionsTests` cases passed, including Unix-only double quotes/wildcards, literal percent sequences, trailing-separator quote wrapping, absent output, and raw `-p:` syntax. [CLI shard 5 TRX](https://helixr1107v0xdeko0k025g8.blob.core.windows.net/dotnet-sdk-refs-pull-56972-merge-e58c2099d21f4603a3/dotnet.Tests.dll.5/1/dotnet.Tests_net12.0_x64.trx?helixlogtype=result) — 465 passed, 0 failed, 1 unrelated skip.
- Existing build/publish/clean/store/VSTest invocation coverage passed in CLI shard 4: 334 passed, 0 failed, 24 OS skips.
- Linux managed/AOT and Windows arm64 AOT builds passed. Markdown links and `git diff --check` passed.

Broader multi-platform CI, including Windows filesystem execution, is still in progress; this PR remains a draft. The local cold redist build was stopped to honor a shared-machine memory-safety hold, so the rebuilt-SDK regression evidence above comes from PR CI rather than a local run.

Issues.Title: Preserve template package source-mapping error details
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #56871.

- Preserve nonempty `PackageNotFound` installer diagnostics in `dotnet new install` and the shared update-result display. Use the existing neutral installation-failure heading instead of incorrectly saying the package does not exist; keep the existing fallback for absent diagnostics.

Package source mapping enforcement and exit codes are unchanged. Existing localized resources are reused.

Both fixed builds completed with zero warnings and zero errors. TRX and binlogs are retained under `artifacts/log/test-runs`. Issues.Title: Respect IsPublishable in Web SDK publish hooks
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #50139.

MSBuild still schedules `AfterTargets="Publish"` hooks when the base `Publish` target is skipped. The Web SDK therefore runs its post-publish dependency chain for `IsPublishable=false`, including `_TransformWebConfig`, which fails when no publish directory exists.

Require `IsPublishable=true` at both Web SDK CLI hook entry points and at the separate `DeployOnBuild` entry point. This skips their complete dependency chains, including transformations, publish-profile execution, and publish callbacks, rather than suppressing a transformation error. The base `Publish` target and project-reference copying are unchanged.

Add 18 regression cases covering Web/Worker SDKs; project, command-line, and profile opt-outs; mixed solutions; ordinary and profile-based successful web publishing; `DeployOnBuild`; absence of publish/intermediate/hook side effects; and preservation of existing publish output.

## Validation

- **Original repro confirmed:** `dotnet new web` followed by `dotnet publish /p:IsPublishable=false -bl` fails with `MSB4018` / `DirectoryNotFoundException` on the unmodified Windows SDK `10.0.300-preview.0.26177.108`.
- **Windows source-target matrix: 18/18 passed.** Repeated the project/CLI/profile opt-outs for Web and Worker projects, mixed-solution normal/profile publishing, both publish and `DeployOnBuild`, and preservation of existing output. Commands ran sequentially with `/m:1` and used the exact three entry-target definitions extracted from this branch as an overlay on the installed SDK. This is source-target validation, not a local rebuilt redist test run.
- **Rebuilt-SDK CI: 21/21 Web SDK tests passed**, including all 18 new regression cases, in the Linux x64 Helix work item from [build 1668339](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1668339). Verified each new test's `Passed` outcome in the uploaded TRX; the [work-item console](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/84c3c628-0668-4fd4-908d-981811d32196/workitems/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web.Tests.dll/console) reports 21 total and zero failures.
- The broader multi-platform CI pipeline is still in progress; the Windows Web SDK test work item was still waiting at the time of this update. No claim that all CI is green.

Issues.Title: Forward LangVersion when compiling satellite assemblies
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Forward `$(LangVersion)` to the `Csc` task in `CoreGenerateSatelliteAssemblies`, matching the project's primary compilation. This fixes localized-resource builds that require `LangVersion=preview` instead of silently compiling satellites with the compiler's default language version.

Add a data-driven regression that reads actual compiler calls from the build binlog, selects the satellite compilation explicitly, and compares its `/langversion:` argument with the primary compilation. Fixes #56839.

Issues.Title: [wasm] Require the browser workload when CoreCLR sets WasmRunWasmOpt
Issues.Body:
Ports the workload-requirement condition from dotnet/runtime#136772 into the SDK's copy of the Mono toolchain workload manifest. This is the copy the SDK actually ships.

CoreCLR browser runs wasm-opt from the wasm-tools workload's Emscripten SDK, both over the relinked `dotnet.native.wasm` (dotnet/runtime#136771) and over the per-app ReadyToRun images (dotnet/runtime#136772). This change adds `WasmRunWasmOpt=true` to `_WasmNativeWorkloadNeeded` for CoreCLR (`UseMonoRuntime=false`), so setting the property marks the workload as required, just like the existing relink triggers. Mono is unchanged: there, `WasmRunWasmOpt` already follows `WasmNativeStrip`, which is a trigger.

Validation (in dotnet/runtime, against the runtime copy of this file with the same change): evaluating a CoreCLR browser project with the workload marked unavailable gives `_WasmNativeWorkloadNeeded=true` and `UsingBrowserRuntimeWorkload=true` when `WasmRunWasmOpt=true`. Without the property, or with `UseMonoRuntime=true`, both stay off. Not built or tested in this repo.

Kept as a draft until dotnet/runtime#136771 and dotnet/runtime#136772 merge.

Issues.Title: [Copilot agent] Watch.Aspire status pipe: populate error, add no_changes/apply_blocked/file_changed, elapsedMs, and a replica id in process_* events
Issues.Body:
[Copilot agent]

Related: microsoft/aspire#21821

### Context

microsoft/aspire#21821 (draft) adds `aspire run --watch` hot reload for C# project resources. It runs `Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire` 10.0.403 in `server` mode with `--status-pipe` and `--control-pipe`. Aspire now drives its dashboard state and terminal notices **only** from the status-pipe JSON. It no longer parses the watcher's console output, which isn't a contract and changes between versions. That costs users some information the console has but the status pipe doesn't. These additions would let a host restore it without scraping.

What 10.0.403 emits today (`WatchStatusEvent`): `type` (`building`, `build_complete`, `hot_reload_applied`, `restarting`, `process_started`, `process_exited`), `projects`, `success`, `error` and `exitCode`.

### Asks

1. **Populate `error` on `build_complete` with `success: false`.** The property exists, but `StatusReportingLoggerFactory` never sets it, so a host can only say "build failed, see the logs". The first diagnostic (or the first N), e.g. `Program.cs(19,32): error CS1525: ...`, would be enough.
2. **Distinguish the outcomes of an apply attempt.** `hot_reload_applied` (`ChangesAppliedToProjectsNotification`) is emitted after every attempt: deltas applied, no code changes (e.g. `appsettings.json`, static files, a revert), or blocked by compile errors. During rebuild cycles it is also emitted with `projects: []`. Requested:
   - `no_changes`: changed files had no code to apply;
   - `apply_blocked`: the change wasn't applied because of compile errors (ideally with `error`);
   - `file_changed`: the changed file paths (or a `files` property on the apply events), so a host can say "(Greeter.cs)".
3. **`elapsedMs`** on `build_complete` and `hot_reload_applied`, so hosts can report apply latency.
4. **A request/replica id echoed in `process_started` and `process_exited`.** With several launch requests for the same project (Aspire `WithReplicas(n)`), `process_*` events only name the project, so a host can't tell which replica started or crashed. An opaque id supplied in the resource-pipe launch request and echoed back (or the process id, plus the launch request id) would fix that.

### Related observation (no change requested)

The control-pipe `{"type":"rebuild","projects":[...]}` command doesn't build in 10.0.403. It emits `restarting` and relaunches the running processes of those projects (`--no-build`, earlier deltas replayed), and skips crashed ones. We use it for the dashboard Restart, and the name surprised us. A note in the docs, or a `build` flag, would help.

Separately, after a project-file change (e.g. an added `PackageReference`) the watcher re-evaluates and restores but doesn't rebuild or relaunch. A later code edit that uses the package then fails at run time (`FileNotFoundException`). Aspire works around this by restarting the watcher on project-file changes.

---
**🤖 Posted by Spiker (AI Agent)**

Issues.Title: Add --format <table|json> support to dotnet new list
Issues.Body:
﻿Fixes #43679

### Summary
Adds support for `--format <table|json>` (defaulting to `table`) on `dotnet new list` following the versioned JSON contract proposed in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/43679#issuecomment-2411579413 and the review feedback in #44140:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "data": [
    {
      "name": "ASP.NET Core Empty",
      "shortNames": ["web"],
      "languages": [ { "id": "C#", "default": true }, { "id": "F#", "default": false } ],
      "types": ["project"],
      "authors": ["Microsoft"],
      "classifications": ["Web", "Empty"]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Changes
- Added `NewListOutputFormat` (`table`, `json`) and `FormatOption` (`--format`, `ArgumentArity.ExactlyOne`, default `table`) to `NewListCommandDefinition`, reusing existing `CommandDefinitionStrings.FormatDescription`.
- Added source-generated `TemplateListJsonSerializerContext` (`JsonSerializerContext` with `JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping` for AOT compatibility and unescaped `#` in `"C#"` / `"F#"`) and `TemplateListJsonContract` in `Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli`.
- Updated `TemplateListCoordinator` and `TemplateGroupDisplay` to emit clean JSON to stdout when `--format json` is specified, without the human-readable banner header.
- Updated Verify approval snapshots (`TabCompletionTests.List_GetAllSuggestions.verified.txt` and `DotnetNewHelpTests.CanShowHelp_List_common.verified.txt`) and added unit and integration tests (`ListTests`, `TabularOutputTests`, `DotnetNewListTests`).

Issues.Title: .NET October 2026 out-of-band security updates
Issues.Body:
On October 25, 2026, we released out-of-band security updates for .NET 8.0.33, .NET 9.0.22, .NET 10.0.14, and .NET 11 Release Candidate 3 (prerelease). We recommend updating affected applications and build environments as soon as possible. .NET Framework is not affected.

## Release Notes

* [Release details and feedback](https://github.com/dotnet/core/issues/10660)
* [.NET 8.0.33 and .NET SDK 8.0.133 / 8.0.427](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.33/8.0.33.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0))
* [.NET 9.0.22 and .NET SDK 9.0.123 / 9.0.320](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.22/9.0.22.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/9.0))
* [.NET 10.0.14 and .NET SDK 10.0.114 / 10.0.403](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.14/10.0.14.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0))
* [.NET 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 and .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 (prerelease)](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc3/11.0.0-rc.3.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0))

## Security advisories

| Advisory | Applicability | Announcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [CVE-2026-111497](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-p3jp-9v83-76w9) | Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write; all platforms when processing untrusted Brotli data. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/494) |
| [CVE-2026-114148](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-r6pf-x897-gm86) | Linux archive ownership; distribution-specific ASP.NET Core archives and source-build engineering inputs. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/495) |
| [CVE-2026-70197](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj) | Windows sockets memory corruption; corrected October 13 fix. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/493) |
| [CVE-2026-102870](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-g27p-qf6j-c96c) | Standalone Blazor WebAssembly debugger packages on .NET 10/11; corrected October 13 fix. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/492) |

The October 13 updates did not fully address CVE-2026-70197 and CVE-2026-102870. These out-of-band updates provide the corrected fixes; the original advisory identities and revision history are preserved. For CVE-2026-102870, update the affected standalone Server/DevServer package references; updating only the shared runtime is not a substitute.

For CVE-2026-114148, affected Microsoft-published .NET 8/9 ASP.NET Core runtime and targeting-pack tarball installations require a clean replacement following the advisory. Source-built archives are build/engineering inputs, not directly deployed production runtimes. Update those inputs and recreate their extracted workspaces using ownership-controlled extraction; review and rebuild affected downstream outputs as needed. .NET 10/11 applicability is limited to source-built distributions.

Also announced at [.NET October 2026 Out-of-Band Security Updates](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/dotnet-october-2026-oob-security-updates/).

Please use the [release feedback issue](https://github.com/dotnet/core/issues/10660) for release-wide issues and the linked per-CVE discussions for advisory questions.
